question: After the death of Moses the servant of the LORD, to whom did the LORD speak to lead Israel?
opt1: Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister
opt2: Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite
opt3: Eleazar the priest, Aaron's successor
opt4: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
correct: Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister
explanation: Following the death of Moses on Mount Nebo, God personally commissioned Joshua as the divine successor to lead the congregation into the promised land. Joshua 1:1 (KJV) - "Now after the death of Moses the servant of the LORD it came to pass, that the LORD spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister, saying,"

question: What river did the LORD command Joshua and all the people to arise and cross over?
opt1: The river Euphrates
opt2: The river Jordan
opt3: The river of Egypt (Nile)
opt4: The river Tigris
correct: The river Jordan
explanation: The Jordan River was the final geographical barrier between the wilderness and Canaan. God commanded the entire host to cross over and possess the land. Joshua 1:2 (KJV) - "Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Israel."

question: What promise did God give to Joshua concerning every place where the sole of their foot should tread?
opt1: Every territory must first be purchased from the Canaanites with silver
opt2: Only the mountainous regions would be given, while the valleys remained foreign
opt3: Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you
opt4: The land would remain an uninhabited wilderness until three generations passed
correct: Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you
explanation: God reaffirmed the Abrahamic covenant to Joshua, assuring that active faith and obedience in stepping out would possess the promised inheritance. Joshua 1:3 (KJV) - "Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you, as I said unto Moses."

question: What assurance did the LORD give Joshua regarding his enemies and God's abiding presence?
opt1: Thou shalt suffer defeat in the early battles before gaining victory
opt2: Canaanite kings would surrender willingly without any conflict or warfare
opt3: Victory would be granted only if forty thousand mercenary archers were hired
opt4: There shall not any man be able to stand before thee all the days of thy life
correct: There shall not any man be able to stand before thee all the days of thy life
explanation: God promised Joshua unfailing divine presence and complete protection against all adversaries throughout his entire leadership. Joshua 1:5 (KJV) - "There shall not any man be able to stand before thee all the days of thy life: as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee: I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee."

question: What encouraging exhortation did the LORD repeatedly give unto Joshua in chapter 1?
opt1: Be strong and of a good courage
opt2: Fear the chariots of iron of the Canaanites
opt3: Return back unto the wilderness of Egypt
opt4: Tarry forty more years until a new generation rises
correct: Be strong and of a good courage
explanation: God commanded Joshua to banish fear and embrace steadfast courage, because divine strength is rooted in God's promises. Joshua 1:6 (KJV) - "Be strong and of a good courage: for unto this people shalt thou divide for an inheritance the land, which I sware unto their fathers to give them."

question: What vital spiritual instruction was given regarding 'this book of the law' in Joshua 1:8?
opt1: The book of the law shall be read publicly only once every seven years at the feast
opt2: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night
opt3: The scroll of the law shall be kept locked within the ark, unseen by the leader
opt4: The words of the law shall be recited only by the high priest during national fasts
correct: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night
explanation: True spiritual prosperity and victory come from constant meditation upon and faithful obedience to God's holy Word day and night. Joshua 1:8 (KJV) - "This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success."

question: Within how many days did Joshua command the people to prepare victuals to pass over Jordan?
opt1: Within seven days
opt2: Within forty days
opt3: Within three days
opt4: Within ten days
correct: Within three days
explanation: Joshua demonstrated decisive faith and immediate readiness, commanding the officers to prepare the camp to cross the flooded Jordan within three days. Joshua 1:11 (KJV) - "Pass through the host, and command the people, saying, Prepare you victuals; for within three days ye shall pass over this Jordan, to go in to possess the land, which the LORD your God giveth you to possess it."

question: Which two and a half tribes were commanded to pass over armed before their brethren until they received rest?
opt1: The tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and the house of Levi
opt2: The tribes of Ephraim, Dan, and the children of Simeon
opt3: The tribes of Zebulun, Naphtali, and the children of Asher
opt4: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh
correct: The Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh
explanation: Although the Reubenites, Gadites, and half tribe of Manasseh received their inheritance east of Jordan, covenant unity required their fighting men to lead the vanguard until all Israel rested. Joshua 1:12-14 (KJV) - "And to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to half the tribe of Manasseh, spake Joshua, saying... Ye shall pass before your brethren armed, all the mighty men of valour, and help them;"

question: Where were the wives, little ones, and cattle of the two and a half tribes to remain during the conquest?
opt1: In the land which Moses gave them on this side Jordan eastward
opt2: In the fortified encampments of Mount Sinai in the south
opt3: In the temporary shelters of Kadesh-barnea under Levite guard
opt4: In the sheltered oases of the wilderness of Paran
correct: In the land which Moses gave them on this side Jordan eastward
explanation: Moses had granted the Transjordan tribes their settlements east of Jordan, where their families and livestock remained protected while their armed warriors fought in Canaan. Joshua 1:14 (KJV) - "Your wives, your little ones, and your cattle, shall remain in the land which Moses gave you on this side Jordan; but ye shall pass before your brethren armed, all the mighty men of valour, and help them;"

question: What decree did the eastern tribes make concerning anyone who rebelled against Joshua's commandment?
opt1: He shall be banished unto the wilderness of Moab for forty days
opt2: Whosoever he be that doth rebel against thy commandment... he shall be put to death
opt3: He shall pay a restitution fine of one hundred shekels of silver
opt4: He shall be stripped of his tribal inheritance and made a bondman
correct: Whosoever he be that doth rebel against thy commandment... he shall be put to death
explanation: The people affirmed absolute loyalty to Joshua as God's appointed commander, decreeing capital punishment for open rebellion to preserve holiness and unity. Joshua 1:18 (KJV) - "Whosoever he be that doth rebel against thy commandment, and will not hearken unto thy words in all that thou commandest him, he shall be put to death: only be strong and of a good courage."

question: From which location did Joshua send out two men secretly to view the land, even Jericho?
opt1: From Gilgal
opt2: From Shittim
opt3: From Kadesh-barnea
opt4: From Hebron
correct: From Shittim
explanation: Israel was encamped at Shittim in the plains of Moab when Joshua dispatched two trusted men to scout Jericho and its defenses. Joshua 2:1 (KJV) - "And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot's house, named Rahab, and lodged there."

question: Into whose house did the two spies enter and lodge when they arrived in Jericho?
opt1: The palace of the king of Jericho
opt2: The house of a Canaanite merchant named Jael
opt3: An harlot's house, named Rahab
opt4: The tent of an Egyptian ambassador
correct: An harlot's house, named Rahab
explanation: God guided the spies to the house of Rahab, a woman whose heart was receptive to the fear of the true God and whose faith would preserve her family. Joshua 2:1 (KJV) - "And they went, and came into an harlot's house, named Rahab, and lodged there."

question: Where did Rahab conceal the two spies when the king of Jericho sent officers to capture them?
opt1: In an empty water cistern beneath her courtyard
opt2: Underneath her bed within the inner chamber
opt3: In a concealed grain cellar outside the city wall
opt4: With the stalks of flax on the roof of her house
correct: With the stalks of flax on the roof of her house
explanation: Rahab protected the Hebrew spies at great personal risk by concealing them under drying stalks of flax arranged on her rooftop. Joshua 2:6 (KJV) - "But she had brought them up to the roof of the house, and hid them with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof."

question: What miracle of the LORD did Rahab say had caused fear to fall upon all the inhabitants of Canaan?
opt1: How the LORD dried up the water of the Red sea for you when ye came out of Egypt
opt2: How manna fell from heaven during the wilderness wanderings
opt3: How the sun stood still in the middle of heaven at Gibeon
opt4: How thunder and lightning shook the heights of Mount Sinai
correct: How the LORD dried up the water of the Red sea for you when ye came out of Egypt
explanation: Rahab testified that the miraculous drying of the Red Sea forty years earlier had struck dread and trembling into the hearts of all Canaanites. Joshua 2:10 (KJV) - "For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed."

question: Which two Amorite kings east of Jordan did Rahab identify as having been utterly destroyed by Israel?
opt1: Balak and Balaam
opt2: Sihon and Og
opt3: Agag and Hadadezer
opt4: Abimelech and Phichol
correct: Sihon and Og
explanation: The decisive defeat of Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan proved that no earthly fortress or giant could withstand God's covenant host. Joshua 2:10 (KJV) - "...and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed."

question: What profound confession of faith did Rahab proclaim concerning the God of Israel in Joshua 2:11?
opt1: He is merely one among the mighty desert deities of Sinai
opt2: He is the tribal protector of Israel with power only over water
opt3: The LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath
opt4: His authority is confined to the mountain heights of Gilead
correct: The LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath
explanation: Rahab's magnificent declaration of faith acknowledged the supreme sovereignty of the LORD over both celestial heaven and the earthly realm. Joshua 2:11 (KJV) - "And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath."

question: Where was Rahab's house situated in the city of Jericho?
opt1: In the central square adjacent to the king's fortress
opt2: Near the eastern gate outside the perimeter of the fortifications
opt3: In the lower district beside the public well of the city
opt4: Upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall
correct: Upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall
explanation: Because her home was built into the outer defensive wall of Jericho, she was able to let the spies down safely by a cord through her window. Joshua 2:15 (KJV) - "Then she let them down by a cord through the window: for her house was upon the town wall, and she dwelt upon the wall."

question: What covenant token was Rahab commanded to bind in the window to protect her household?
opt1: This line of scarlet thread in the window
opt2: A consecrated branch of hyssop dipped in blood
opt3: A blue ribbon embroidered with gold filigree
opt4: A white linen banner suspended from the balcony
correct: This line of scarlet thread in the window
explanation: The scarlet cord hanging from Rahab's window served as a prophetic sign of deliverance through blood, ensuring her family was spared when Jericho fell. Joshua 2:18 (KJV) - "Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father's household, home unto thee."

question: How long did Rahab advise the spies to hide in the mountain before returning across Jordan?
opt1: Hide yourselves there seven days until the gates open
opt2: Hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned
opt3: Wait until midnight and immediately swim across the Jordan
opt4: Conceal yourselves for forty days in the wilderness of Judah
correct: Hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned
explanation: Rahab's practical wisdom ensured the spies avoided the Jericho search parties, which combed the Jordan fords for three days before abandoning the chase. Joshua 2:16 (KJV) - "And she said unto them, Get you to the mountain, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned: and afterward may ye go your way."

question: What triumphant report did the two spies deliver to Joshua after returning from Jericho?
opt1: The walls of Jericho reach unto heaven and the giants cannot be overcome
opt2: We must remain at Shittim until the river Jordan recedes during summer
opt3: Truly the LORD hath delivered into our hands all the land; for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us
opt4: The king of Jericho offers a covenant of peace in exchange for tribute
correct: Truly the LORD hath delivered into our hands all the land; for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us
explanation: Unlike the ten unbelieving spies at Kadesh-barnea, these two faithful spies brought an inspiring testimony of God's victory and the enemy's total terror. Joshua 2:24 (KJV) - "And they said unto Joshua, Truly the LORD hath delivered into our hands all the land; for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us."

question: How much space was commanded to be kept between the ark of the covenant and the people of Israel?
opt1: Fifty cubits by measure
opt2: Five hundred cubits by measure
opt3: About two thousand cubits by measure
opt4: One hundred cubits by measure
correct: About two thousand cubits by measure
explanation: A reverence distance of about two thousand cubits (approx. 3,000 feet) allowed the entire host to see and follow the ark as it led them through the uncharted waters. Joshua 3:4 (KJV) - "Yet there shall be a space between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure: come not near unto it, that ye may know the way by which ye must go: for ye have not passed this way heretofore."

question: What spiritual preparation did Joshua command the people to make before the crossing of Jordan?
opt1: Fast for forty days and wear sackcloth before the priests
opt2: Sharpen all bronze swords and prepare shields for immediate battle
opt3: Collect offerings of gold and silver to build an altar on the shore
opt4: Sanctify yourselves: for to morrow the LORD will do wonders among you
correct: Sanctify yourselves: for to morrow the LORD will do wonders among you
explanation: God requires personal holiness and spiritual consecration before displaying His supernatural wonder-working power among His people. Joshua 3:5 (KJV) - "And Joshua said unto the people, Sanctify yourselves: for to morrow the LORD will do wonders among you."

question: Who was commanded to carry the ark of the covenant and pass over before the congregation?
opt1: The priests that bare the ark of the covenant
opt2: The seventy elders representing the twelve tribes
opt3: Joshua and the mighty men of valour from Judah
opt4: The sons of Gershon carrying the tabernacle coverings
correct: The priests that bare the ark of the covenant
explanation: The priests bearing the sacred ark of God's presence led the way, demonstrating that God Himself went before His people to open the path. Joshua 3:6 (KJV) - "And Joshua spake unto the priests, saying, Take up the ark of the covenant, and pass over before the people. And they took up the ark of the covenant, and went before the people."

question: What did the LORD promise to do for Joshua on the day of crossing the Jordan?
opt1: Bestow upon him a royal golden crown as king over the nation
opt2: This day will I begin to magnify thee in the sight of all Israel
opt3: Exalt his lineage so his sons would govern Israel in perpetuity
opt4: Give him dominion over the empires of Egypt and Assyria
correct: This day will I begin to magnify thee in the sight of all Israel
explanation: God confirmed Joshua's spiritual authority in the sight of all Israel, just as He had previously validated Moses at the Red Sea. Joshua 3:7 (KJV) - "And the LORD said unto Joshua, This day will I begin to magnify thee in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that, as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee."

question: Where were the priests bearing the ark commanded to stand when they reached the Jordan?
opt1: They were to swim to the western shore and erect a signal fire
opt2: They were to set the ark upon an altar of stones on the eastern bank
opt3: When ye are come to the brink of the water of Jordan, ye shall stand still in Jordan
opt4: They were to retreat twenty paces until the current slowed down
correct: When ye are come to the brink of the water of Jordan, ye shall stand still in Jordan
explanation: Faith required the priests to step directly into the rushing waters while the river was still at flood stage, trusting God to part the waters. Joshua 3:8 (KJV) - "And thou shalt command the priests that bear the ark of the covenant, saying, When ye are come to the brink of the water of Jordan, ye shall stand still in Jordan."

question: How many men was Joshua commanded to select out of the tribes of Israel, out of every tribe a man?
opt1: Seventy men representing the council of elders
opt2: Twenty-four men chosen from the house of Aaron
opt3: Forty men selected from the mighty men of war
opt4: Twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, out of every tribe a man
correct: Twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, out of every tribe a man
explanation: Twelve men, one representing each tribe, were designated to perform a special covenant memorial task during the miraculous river crossing. Joshua 3:12 (KJV) - "Now therefore take you twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, out of every tribe a man."

question: What miracle occurred the moment the feet of the priests bearing the ark were dipped in the brim of Jordan?
opt1: The waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap
opt2: A bridge of solid granite formed across the expanse of the river
opt3: The waters turned into sweet milk for the entire congregation to drink
opt4: A sudden drought dried up all the mountain springs in Gilead
correct: The waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap
explanation: As an immediate response to obedient faith, the flooded waters upstream were supernatural halted, rising up in a great wall while the downstream flow drained completely. Joshua 3:15-16 (KJV) - "And as they that bare the ark were come unto Jordan, and the feet of the priests that bare the ark were dipped in the brim of the water... That the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap..."

question: Near which city did the upstream waters rise up upon an heap very far off?
opt1: The fortress of Jerusalem beside Mount Moriah
opt2: The city Adam, that is beside Zaretan
opt3: The royal city of Hazor in the northern valley
opt4: The ancient town of Bethlehem in the hill country
correct: The city Adam, that is beside Zaretan
explanation: The biblical narrative records precise geographical historical accuracy: the waters piled up miles upstream near the city of Adam beside Zaretan. Joshua 3:16 (KJV) - "That the waters which came down from above stood and rose up upon an heap very far from the city Adam, that is beside Zaretan: and those that came down toward the sea of the plain, even the salt sea, failed, and were cut off: and the people passed over right against Jericho."

question: What was the hydrological condition of the river Jordan at the time of Israel's crossing?
opt1: The river was at its lowest summer drought level
opt2: The river was frozen solid by unseasonal winter frost
opt3: Jordan overfloweth all his banks all the time of harvest
opt4: The river flowed only in underground subterranean channels
correct: Jordan overfloweth all his banks all the time of harvest
explanation: The miracle was magnified because the crossing took place in the spring harvest season when snowmelt from Mount Hermon caused Jordan to overflow all its banks. Joshua 3:15 (KJV) - "(for Jordan overfloweth all his banks all the time of harvest,)"

question: On what kind of ground did the priests bearing the ark stand firm while all Israel passed over?
opt1: They stood sinking in deep riverbed mud up to their loins
opt2: They stood upon a floating raft of acacia logs
opt3: They stood on stone pillars raised by the Canaanites
opt4: The priests stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan
correct: The priests stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan
explanation: God completely dried the riverbed, providing dry, firm ground for the millions of Israelites to cross over cleanly and swiftly into the land of promise. Joshua 3:17 (KJV) - "And the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan, and all the Israelites passed over on dry ground, until all the people were passed clean over Jordan."

question: How many stones were the twelve appointed men commanded to take out of the midst of Jordan?
opt1: Seven stones representing the days of creation
opt2: Ten stones representing the commandments of Moses
opt3: Forty stones representing the years in the wilderness
opt4: Twelve stones, according unto the number of the tribes of Israel
correct: Twelve stones, according unto the number of the tribes of Israel
explanation: Twelve stones were gathered from the dry riverbed, each symbolizing one of the twelve tribes of Israel united under God's covenant grace. Joshua 4:3 (KJV) - "And command ye them, saying, Take you hence out of the midst of Jordan, out of the place where the priests' feet stood firm, twelve stones, and ye shall carry them over with you, and leave them in the lodging place, where ye shall lodge this night."

question: From what exact location in the Jordan riverbed were the twelve stones to be taken?
opt1: Out of the place where the priests' feet stood firm
opt2: From the shallow eastern shore where the spies stood
opt3: From the western bank near the palms of Jericho
opt4: From the deep natural caves along the northern riverbank
correct: Out of the place where the priests' feet stood firm
explanation: The memorial stones had to come directly from the sacred spot where the priests' feet stood firm under the ark, where God held back the surging waters. Joshua 4:3 (KJV) - "Take you hence out of the midst of Jordan, out of the place where the priests' feet stood firm, twelve stones..."

question: How were the twelve men instructed to carry the stones out of the midst of Jordan?
opt1: Carried in large linen sacks upon pack donkeys
opt2: Take ye up every man of you a stone upon his shoulder
opt3: Transported on two-wheeled wooden ox carts
opt4: Dragged along the ground with cords of flax
correct: Take ye up every man of you a stone upon his shoulder
explanation: Each representative carried a substantial stone upon his own shoulder, demonstrating personal dedication to carrying the memorial of God's miraculous power. Joshua 4:5 (KJV) - "And Joshua said unto them, Pass over before the ark of the LORD your God into the midst of Jordan, and take ye up every man of you a stone upon his shoulder, according unto the number of the tribes of the children of Israel:"

question: Where else did Joshua set up twelve stones besides the memorial monument at Gilgal?
opt1: On the highest peak of Mount Nebo overlooking the plains
opt2: At the eastern gate of Jericho beside the palm trees
opt3: In the midst of Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests which bare the ark stood
opt4: In the valley of Achor beneath a great mound of rocks
correct: In the midst of Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests which bare the ark stood
explanation: Joshua established a second monument of twelve stones submerged in the riverbed itself, marking the exact spot where the ark of God stopped the waters. Joshua 4:9 (KJV) - "And Joshua set up twelve stones in the midst of Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests which bare the ark of the covenant stood: and they are there unto this day."

question: About how many armed men from the Transjordan tribes passed over before the LORD unto battle?
opt1: Ten thousand valiant archers
opt2: One hundred thousand armed warriors
opt3: Five thousand chosen spear-men
opt4: About forty thousand prepared for war passed over
correct: About forty thousand prepared for war passed over
explanation: True to their sacred promise to Moses and Joshua, approximately forty thousand elite warriors from Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh crossed in front of their brethren into the plains of Jericho. Joshua 4:13 (KJV) - "About forty thousand prepared for war passed over before the LORD unto battle, to the plains of Jericho."

question: What happened to the waters of Jordan when the priests carrying the ark stepped onto the dry bank?
opt1: The waters of Jordan returned unto their place, and overflowed all his banks, as they did before
opt2: The riverbed remained dry and empty for forty more days
opt3: The river permanently diverted its course into the Great Sea
opt4: The waters surged backward and flooded the city of Shittim
correct: The waters of Jordan returned unto their place, and overflowed all his banks, as they did before
explanation: The moment the soles of the priests' feet touched the shore, God released the held-back waters, proving that God's presence alone controlled the mighty river. Joshua 4:18 (KJV) - "And it came to pass... that the waters of Jordan returned unto their place, and overflowed all his banks, as they did before."

question: On what precise biblical calendar date did the people come up out of Jordan and encamp in Gilgal?
opt1: On the first day of the seventh month
opt2: On the tenth day of the first month
opt3: On the fifteenth day of the second month
opt4: On the twentieth day of the third month
correct: On the tenth day of the first month
explanation: The crossing took place on the tenth day of Abib (Nisan), the exact day when the Passover lamb was selected according to Exodus 12, pointing to divine redemption. Joshua 4:19 (KJV) - "And the people came up out of Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamped in Gilgal, in the east border of Jericho."

question: Where did Joshua pitch the twelve memorial stones taken from the midst of Jordan?
opt1: In Bethel on the mountain heights
opt2: In Shiloh before the tabernacle
opt3: In Gilgal, in the east border of Jericho
opt4: In Shechem between the twin mountains
correct: In Gilgal, in the east border of Jericho
explanation: Gilgal became Israel's primary military headquarters and spiritual base camp, where the twelve stones stood as an enduring witness of God's covenant power. Joshua 4:20 (KJV) - "And those twelve stones, which they took out of Jordan, did Joshua pitch in Gilgal."

question: What were parents commanded to tell their children in time to come when asked, 'What mean these stones?'
opt1: These stones were boundary markers set by ancient Canaanite kings
opt2: These rocks are the ruins of an ancient altar built by Melchizedek
opt3: These pillars represent the burial cairns of thirty-six fallen soldiers
opt4: Israel came over this Jordan on dry land, for the LORD your God dried up the waters
correct: Israel came over this Jordan on dry land, for the LORD your God dried up the waters
explanation: God instituted the stone memorial so that succeeding generations would be taught the living testimony of God's miraculous deliverance and faithfulness. Joshua 4:21-22 (KJV) - "...When your children shall ask their fathers in time to come, saying, What mean these stones? Then ye shall let your children know, saying, Israel came over this Jordan on dry land."

question: According to Joshua 4:24, what was the ultimate global purpose of this miraculous river crossing?
opt1: That all the people of the earth might know the hand of the LORD, that it is mighty: that ye might fear the LORD your God for ever
opt2: To establish Joshua as an earthly monarch over the surrounding nations
opt3: To amass immense tributes of gold and silver from the coastal kings
opt4: To prove that Israel possessed superior military technology and tactics
correct: That all the people of the earth might know the hand of the LORD, that it is mighty: that ye might fear the LORD your God for ever
explanation: The ultimate goal of God's supernatural deeds was evangelistic and doxological: that all nations would recognize the almighty power of the LORD and revere Him forever. Joshua 4:24 (KJV) - "That all the people of the earth might know the hand of the LORD, that it is mighty: that ye might fear the LORD your God for ever."

question: What psychological effect did the crossing of Jordan have on all the kings of the Amorites and Canaanites?
opt1: Their heart melted, neither was there spirit in them any more, because of the children of Israel
opt2: They mobilized an allied force of fifty thousand iron chariots
opt3: They immediately surrendered their fortresses and embraced Israel's God
opt4: They sailed in ships across the Great Sea to find refuge in Egypt
correct: Their heart melted, neither was there spirit in them any more, because of the children of Israel
explanation: When the pagan kings heard how God had dried up the swollen Jordan, overwhelming terror paralyzed their wills and shattered their courage. Joshua 5:1 (KJV) - "...that their heart melted, neither was there spirit in them any more, because of the children of Israel."

question: What instrument did the LORD command Joshua to make to circumcise the children of Israel at Gilgal?
opt1: Swords forged of tempered bronze
opt2: Sharp knives of flint
opt3: Shears fashioned from polished brass
opt4: Razors beaten out of pure gold
correct: Sharp knives of flint
explanation: God commanded the use of sharp flint knives to renew the covenant sign of circumcision before Israel engaged in holy warfare for the promised land. Joshua 5:2 (KJV) - "At that time the LORD said unto Joshua, Make thee sharp knives, and circumcise again the children of Israel the second time."

question: Why had the generation born in the wilderness during the forty years not been circumcised?
opt1: Moses had forbidden circumcision while the cloud moved by day
opt2: There were no stone quarries or flint deposits in the Sinai peninsula
opt3: All the people that were born in the wilderness by the way... them they had not circumcised
opt4: The law of circumcision had been replaced by the pillar of fire
correct: All the people that were born in the wilderness by the way... them they had not circumcised
explanation: During the forty years of wandering under divine judgment, the wilderness generation had neglected the covenant sign of circumcision until renewed at Gilgal. question: Whom did Joshua encounter standing near Jericho with a drawn sword in His hand?

question: What battle plan did the LORD give Joshua for marching around Jericho on the first six days?
opt1: Attack the eastern gates at midnight with battering rams and flaming arrows

question: What were the seven priests instructed to bear before the ark of the covenant?

Joshua 6:4 (KJV) - "And seven priests shall bear before the ark seven trumpets of rams' horns: and the seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times, and the priests shall blow with the trumpets."

question: How many times was the host commanded to march around the city on the seventh day?

explanation: On the climactic seventh day, the marching intensified sevenfold, beginning early at dawn to fulfill God's complete and perfect work of judgment. Joshua 6:4 (KJV) - "...and the seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times, and the priests shall blow with the trumpets."

question: What strict instruction did Joshua give the people regarding their voices during the marching on the first six days?
opt1: Chant the songs of Moses continually while marching around the wall

Joshua 6:10 (KJV) - "And Joshua had commanded the people, saying, Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout."

Joshua 6:23, 25 (KJV) - "...and they brought out all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel... and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day; because she hid the messengers, which Joshua sent to spy out Jericho."

question: What solemn curse did Joshua pronounce upon anyone who would attempt to rebuild the city of Jericho?

Joshua 6:26 (KJV) - "And Joshua adjured them at that time, saying, Cursed be the man before the LORD, that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho: he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it."

question: What specific divine signal was Joshua commanded to give to trigger the hidden ambush?

explanation: Jericho stood as the firstfruits fortress conquered west of Jordan through miraculous divine power. Joshua 12:9 (KJV) - "The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;"

question: Which city's ruler was listed as the thirty-first and final king conquered in Joshua 12:24?
opt1: The king of Megiddo, one
opt2: The king of Tirzah, one
opt3: The king of Gezer, one
opt4: The king of Jokneam of Carmel, one
correct: The king of Tirzah, one
explanation: Tirzah, later renowned for its exceptional beauty and northern royal residence (Song 6:4, 1 Kings 14:17), completes the catalog of thirty-one defeated kingdoms. Joshua 12:24 (KJV) - "The king of Tirzah, one: all the kings thirty and one."

question: In what diverse geographical terrains did the thirty-one defeated Canaanite kings rule?
opt1: Exclusively along the sandy maritime coastline of the Great Sea
opt2: Solely within the barren dunes of the desert wilderness of Zin
opt3: In the mountains, and in the valleys, and in the plains, and in the springs, and in the wilderness, and in the south country
opt4: In subterranean limestone caverns beneath the heights of Carmel
correct: In the mountains, and in the valleys, and in the plains, and in the springs, and in the wilderness, and in the south country
explanation: God demonstrated His absolute supremacy over every earthly ecosystem: whether high mountains, deep valleys, fertile plains, or arid deserts, no fortress could resist His power. Joshua 12:8 (KJV) - "In the mountains, and in the valleys, and in the plains, and in the springs, and in the wilderness, and in the south country; the Hittites, the Amorites, and the Canaanites..."

question: Which king of Gezer marched to assist Lachish and was smitten by Joshua (noted in Josh 12:12)?
opt1: Jabin king of Hazor, slain at the waters of Merom
opt2: Piram king of Jarmuth, captured in the cave of Makkedah
opt3: Hoham king of Hebron, defeated at the battle of Gibeon
opt4: Horam king of Gezer, smitten when he came up to help Lachish
correct: Horam king of Gezer, smitten when he came up to help Lachish
explanation: Horam made a futile military sortie to relieve the siege of Lachish, resulting in the total destruction of his forces and city. Joshua 12:12 (KJV) - "The king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;" (cf. Joshua 10:33 - "Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish; and Joshua smote him and his people, until he had left him none remaining.")

question: What is the primary spiritual significance of the catalog of 31 defeated kings in Joshua 12?
opt1: A legal, historical testimony of God's absolute faithfulness in fulfilling His covenant promise to give the land of Canaan unto Abraham's seed
opt2: A military invoice designed to extract annual war reparations from neighbouring empires
opt3: An imperial blueprint for Joshua's descendants to establish a hereditary royal dynasty
opt4: A catalog of pagan shrines to be preserved as historical monuments for foreign visitors
correct: A legal, historical testimony of God's absolute faithfulness in fulfilling His covenant promise to give the land of Canaan unto Abraham's seed
explanation: Chapter 12 stands as a monumental legal deed and praise record, verifying that God's covenant promises spoken centuries earlier to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob were fulfilled to the letter. Joshua 12:1, 24 (KJV) - It records the faithful fulfillment of God's covenant promise to give the land of Canaan unto Abraham's seed.

question: What divine assessment did the LORD give to Joshua at the opening of chapter 13?
opt1: Thou art old and stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed
opt2: Thou hast completed every battle and mayest now build a royal palace in Jericho
opt3: Lead the twelve tribes across the southern border into the empire of Egypt
opt4: Appoint twelve kings over the conquered cities to extract annual tributes of gold
correct: Thou art old and stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed
explanation: Even after decades of faithful warfare, God reminded the aging Joshua that significant regions still awaited possession, urging the nation to continue claiming their inheritance by faith. Joshua 13:1 (KJV) - "Now Joshua was old and stricken in years; and the LORD said unto him, Thou art old and stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed."

question: Which five lords of the Philistines ruled territories that still remained unconquered in Joshua 13:3?
opt1: The kings of Tyre, Sidon, Byblos, Arvad, and Berytus along the northern coast
opt2: The Gazathites, the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites
opt3: The rulers of Moab, Ammon, Edom, Amalek, and Midian in the eastern wilderness
opt4: The five Amorite monarchs who previously fled into the cave of Makkedah
correct: The Gazathites, the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites
explanation: The Philistine Pentapolis (five major coastal city-states: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron) remained an unconquered southwest stronghold that would test Israel in subsequent generations. Joshua 13:3 (KJV) - "...five lords of the Philistines; the Gazathites, and the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avites:"

question: To how many western tribes, plus which half tribe, was Joshua commanded to apportion the land west of Jordan?
opt1: Unto all twelve tribes in twelve exactly equal territorial divisions
opt2: Unto seven southern tribes and the priestly family of Aaron
opt3: Unto the nine tribes, and the half tribe of Manasseh
opt4: Unto the tribe of Judah exclusively to rule over their brethren
correct: Unto the nine tribes, and the half tribe of Manasseh
explanation: Because two and a half tribes had already received their portion east of Jordan from Moses, nine and a half tribes remained to receive their inheritances in Canaan proper. Joshua 13:7 (KJV) - "Now therefore divide this land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes, and the half tribe of Manasseh,"

question: Why did the tribe of Levi receive no territorial land inheritance from Moses or Joshua?
opt1: Because their population was too small to defend fortified border towns
opt2: Because they had refused to send armed warriors across the river Jordan
opt3: Because they were condemned to perpetual wandering for building the golden calf
opt4: The sacrifices of the LORD God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance, as he said unto them
correct: The sacrifices of the LORD God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance, as he said unto them
explanation: The Levites possessed the highest, most sacred inheritance: God Himself and the sacred sacrificial offerings of His altar, freeing them to minister spiritually to all twelve tribes. Joshua 13:14, 33 (KJV) - "Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the LORD God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance, as he said unto them... the LORD God of Israel was their inheritance, as he said unto them."

question: Which infamous soothsayer was slain with the sword by Israel among the casualties of war?
opt1: Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword
opt2: Jannes the Egyptian sorcerer who resisted Moses before Pharaoh
opt3: Elymas the sorcerer who sought to turn the deputy from the faith
opt4: Jambres the magician who practiced enchantments in the wilderness
correct: Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword
explanation: Balaam, who had greedily counseled Balak to ensnare Israel in gross immorality and idolatry at Baal-peor (Num 31:16), met divine justice and retribution at the edge of the sword. Joshua 13:22 (KJV) - "Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them."

question: What primary territory was assigned to the tribe of Reuben as their possession east of Jordan?
opt1: The hill country of Judea extending south to the wilderness of Beersheba
opt2: From Aroer on the bank of the river Arnon, the plain by Medeba, and Heshbon with all her cities
opt3: The fertile plain of Sharon stretching from Joppa unto Mount Carmel
opt4: The forested slopes of Mount Hermon reaching unto the sources of Jordan
correct: From Aroer on the bank of the river Arnon, the plain by Medeba, and Heshbon with all her cities
explanation: Reuben received the southernmost Transjordan plateau, encompassing ancient Moabite tablelands and the conquered royal city of Sihon at Heshbon. Joshua 13:15-17 (KJV) - "And their coast was from Aroer, that is on the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain by Medeba; Heshbon, and all her cities that are in the plain;"

question: What pastoral region was granted to the tribe of Gad as their tribal inheritance?
opt1: The desert sands of Kadesh-barnea and the springs of Marah
opt2: The coastal harbor of Accho and the olive groves of Asher
opt3: Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon
opt4: The mountainous ridges of Gilboa and the shores of Chinnereth
correct: Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon
explanation: Gad received central Transjordan, renowned for its rich agricultural pastures, forests of Gilead, and strategic border lands along the Jabbok River. Joshua 13:24-25 (KJV) - "And their coast was Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, unto Aroer that is before Rabbah;"

question: To which specific family of Manasseh was half of Gilead and the kingdom of Og in Bashan granted?
opt1: Unto the sons of Aaron the high priest for priestly pastures
opt2: Unto the family of Caleb the Kenezite for his faithful testimony
opt3: Unto the royal house of Ephraim to oversee northern commerce
opt4: Unto the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even to the one half of the children of Machir
correct: Unto the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even to the one half of the children of Machir
explanation: Because Machir's descendants were valiant men of war who conquered the giant territory of Bashan, Moses awarded them that vast northern region east of Jordan. Joshua 13:31 (KJV) - "And half Gilead, and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were pertained unto the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even to the one half of the children of Machir by their families."

question: In what geographical location did Moses distribute the Transjordan inheritances before his death?
opt1: In the plains of Moab, on the other side Jordan, by Jericho, eastward
opt2: At the foot of Mount Sinai in the wilderness of the south
opt3: In the valley of Eshcol where the cluster of grapes was cut
opt4: At the oasis of Elim beneath the seventy palm trees
correct: In the plains of Moab, on the other side Jordan, by Jericho, eastward
explanation: Moses concluded his earthly ministry by allotting the eastern lands while Israel was encamped opposite Jericho in the plains of Moab. Joshua 13:32 (KJV) - "These are the countries which Moses did distribute for inheritance in the plains of Moab, on the other side Jordan, by Jericho, eastward."

question: According to Joshua 13:33, what was the glorious personal portion given to the tribe of Levi?
opt1: One-tenth of all the gold plundered from the thirty-one kings
opt2: The LORD God of Israel was their inheritance, as he said unto them
opt3: The fortified citadel of Jerusalem as an everlasting sanctuary
opt4: A royal title of nobility inherited by all the sons of Kohath
correct: The LORD God of Israel was their inheritance, as he said unto them
explanation: To have the LORD God Himself as one's inheritance transcends all earthly real estate, prefiguring the believer's eternal spiritual inheritance in Christ. Joshua 13:33 (KJV) - "But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance: the LORD God of Israel was their inheritance, as he said unto them."

question: Who were the primary designated leaders responsible for distributing the land of Canaan by lot?
opt1: The seventy judges of Israel and the captains of the eastern armies
opt2: Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes
opt3: Phinehas the son of Eleazar and the royal princes of the house of Joseph
opt4: Caleb the Kenezite and the twelve scribes appointed from the Levites
correct: Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes
explanation: The distribution was overseen with divine integrity by the high priest Eleazar, the civil leader Joshua, and the hereditary tribal patriarchs before the sanctuary. Joshua 14:1 (KJV) - "And these are the countries which the children of Israel inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed for inheritance unto them."

question: By what divine method was the inheritance apportioned to the nine and a half tribes?
opt1: By personal auction to whichever tribe offered the most silver talents
opt2: By physical combat tournaments held in the plains of Jericho
opt3: By lot was their inheritance, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses
opt4: By seniority of birth order among the twelve sons of Jacob
correct: By lot was their inheritance, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses
explanation: Casting the sacred lot removed all human partiality, jealousy, and political lobbying, submitting the territorial borders directly to God's sovereign appointment (Prov 16:33). Joshua 14:2 (KJV) - "By lot was their inheritance, as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses, for the nine tribes, and for the half tribe."

question: What did the Levites receive instead of a vast contiguous territorial province?
opt1: A walled mountain sanctuary located exclusively in Mount Ephraim
opt2: An island off the Mediterranean coast dedicated to priestly study
opt3: Tents in the central court of each tribal capital without land
opt4: Cities to dwell in, with their suburbs for their cattle and for their substance
correct: Cities to dwell in, with their suburbs for their cattle and for their substance
explanation: God scattered the Levites throughout all the tribes in forty-eight designated cities, placing spiritual teachers and pastoral ministers within reach of every Israelite. Joshua 14:4 (KJV) - "...save cities to dwell in, with their suburbs for their cattle and for their substance."

question: How old was Caleb the son of Jephunneh when Moses sent him from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land?
opt1: Forty years old was I when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea
opt2: Twenty-five years old, in the prime of his youth
opt3: Sixty years old, an elder among the princes of Judah
opt4: Thirty years old, the age of priestly ordination
correct: Forty years old was I when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea
explanation: Caleb recalled his early days of faithful service when at age forty he boldly stood against ten unbelieving spies and declared God's ability to conquer Canaan. Joshua 14:7 (KJV) - "Forty years old was I when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land; and I brought him word again as it was in mine heart."

question: What distinct spiritual commendation was repeatedly declared concerning Caleb's walk with God?
opt1: He offered more burnt sacrifices than all his contemporaries
opt2: I wholly followed the LORD my God
opt3: He built forty altars of unhewn stone throughout the wilderness
opt4: He surpassed all warriors in archery and chariot warfare
correct: I wholly followed the LORD my God
explanation: Caleb's epitaph of enduring honour is that he 'wholly followed the LORD' with unwavering, wholehearted faith, regardless of prevailing cultural unbelief. Joshua 14:8, 9, 14 (KJV) - "...but I wholly followed the LORD my God... because that he wholly followed the LORD God of Israel."

question: How old was Caleb on the day he stood before Joshua requesting his promised inheritance?
opt1: One hundred and ten years old, ready to pass away
opt2: Seventy years old, having completed the wilderness wanderings
opt3: And now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old (85 years old)
opt4: Ninety-nine years old, the age of Abraham's circumcision
correct: And now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old (85 years old)
explanation: After forty-five years of patient waiting and active wilderness journeying, Caleb arrived at age eighty-five with undiminished spiritual zeal and physical vigor. Joshua 14:10 (KJV) - "And now, behold, the LORD hath kept me alive, as he said, these forty and five years... and now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old."

question: What remarkable physical testimony did 85-year-old Caleb proclaim concerning his strength?
opt1: My eyes are dim and my steps are faltering, yet my spirit rejoices in the LORD
opt2: I require twenty young warriors to bear my bronze shield and chariot into battle
opt3: I desire only a quiet resting place in the fertile valley beside the river Jordan
opt4: As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, both to go out, and to come in
correct: As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, both to go out, and to come in
explanation: God supernaturally preserved Caleb's bodily strength and warrior spirit through decades of wilderness hardship because of his uncompromised faith. Joshua 14:11 (KJV) - "As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, both to go out, and to come in."

question: What specific mountain territory did Caleb boldly request Joshua to grant unto him?
opt1: Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the LORD spake in that day... the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced
opt2: Give me the peaceful fertile plains of Jericho beside the palm groves
opt3: Give me the maritime coast of Joppa with its fishing harbors
opt4: Give me the wooded summit of Mount Tabor overlooking the Jezreel valley
correct: Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the LORD spake in that day... the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced
explanation: Instead of seeking an easy retirement, the 85-year-old hero of faith asked for the most formidable stronghold in Canaan—the mountain where the terrifying Anakim giants lived. Joshua 14:12 (KJV) - "Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the LORD spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced: if so be the LORD will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out, as the LORD said."

question: What famous city did Joshua grant unto Caleb for an inheritance with his blessing?
opt1: The ancient fortress of Jerusalem on Mount Zion
opt2: Hebron therefore became the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite unto this day
opt3: The fortified sanctuary city of Shechem in Mount Ephraim
opt4: The royal city of Megiddo in the northern plain
correct: Hebron therefore became the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite unto this day
explanation: Hebron, the sacred burial ground of Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, and Jacob at Machpelah, became the covenant reward for Caleb's unswerving fidelity. Joshua 14:13-14 (KJV) - "And Joshua blessed him, and gave unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh Hebron for an inheritance. Hebron therefore became the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite unto this day..."

question: What was the ancient name of Hebron before Caleb conquered it, and who was it named after?
opt1: Luz, named after the almond trees blooming in the rocky valley
opt2: Salem, named after the ancient king of righteousness Melchizedek
opt3: Kirjath-arba; which Arba was a great man among the Anakims
opt4: Jebus, named after the warrior founders of the mountain fortress
correct: Kirjath-arba; which Arba was a great man among the Anakims
explanation: Hebron had been called Kirjath-arba ('City of Arba'), named after the legendary progenitor and tallest hero among the Anakim giants. Joshua 14:15 (KJV) - "And the name of Hebron before was Kirjath-arba; which Arba was a great man among the Anakims. And the land had rest from war."

question: Which tribe's inheritance was described first in Canaan proper, extending south unto the border of Edom?
opt1: The lot of the tribe of Ephraim the son of Joseph
opt2: The lot of the tribe of Benjamin between the mountains
opt3: The lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families
opt4: The lot of the tribe of Dan along the western seacoast
correct: The lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families
explanation: In accordance with Jacob's blessing that the sceptre would not depart from Judah (Gen 49:10), Judah received the first and largest territorial allotment in southern Canaan. Joshua 15:1 (KJV) - "This then was the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families; even to the border of Edom the wilderness of Zin southward was the uttermost part of the south coast."

question: Which body of water formed the entire eastern boundary of the territory of Judah?
opt1: The Sea of Galilee in the northern hills
opt2: The river of Egypt extending to the desert
opt3: The river Euphrates far to the northeast
opt4: The salt sea, even unto the end of Jordan (the Dead Sea)
correct: The salt sea, even unto the end of Jordan (the Dead Sea)
explanation: The Salt Sea (Dead Sea) served as the natural, unbreachable eastern defensive moat for Judah's mountain heartland. Joshua 15:5 (KJV) - "And the east border was the salt sea, even unto the end of Jordan..."

question: Which great body of water formed the entire western border of Judah's inheritance?
opt1: The great sea (Mediterranean Sea), and the coast thereof
opt2: The river Jordan with its fertile reed banks
opt3: The Sea of Chinnereth with its fishing fleets
opt4: The Red Sea bordering the wilderness of Sinai
correct: The great sea (Mediterranean Sea), and the coast thereof
explanation: Judah's western frontier stretched to the Mediterranean Sea ('The Great Sea'), embracing coastal plains and rolling Shephelah foothills. Joshua 15:12 (KJV) - "And the west border was to the great sea, and the coast thereof. This is the coast of the children of Judah round about according to their families."

question: Which three sons of Anak did Caleb drive out from Hebron through faith and courage?
opt1: Sihon, Og, and Balak, the Amorite rulers
opt2: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak
opt3: Hoham, Piram, and Japhia, the southern kings
opt4: Goliath, Lahmi, and Ishbi-benob, the giants of Gath
correct: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak
explanation: Caleb fearlessly confronted and expelled the three giant chieftains of Anak whose names had terrified an entire generation forty years earlier. Joshua 15:14 (KJV) - "And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak."

question: What reward did Caleb offer to any warrior who would successfully attack and capture Kirjath-sepher (Debir)?
opt1: Ten talents of refined silver and a chariot of bronze
opt2: The perpetual governorship over the southern city of Hebron
opt3: He that smiteth Kirjath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife
opt4: Exemption from all military conscription and tribal taxes
correct: He that smiteth Kirjath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife
explanation: Caleb sought a valiant, faith-filled son-in-law worthy of his daughter Achsah, offering her hand to whoever conquered the fortified city of Kirjath-sepher. Joshua 15:16 (KJV) - "And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife."

question: Who captured Kirjath-sepher and subsequently became the first judge of Israel?
opt1: Shamgar the son of Anath who smote the Philistines
opt2: Gideon the son of Joash the Abiezrite
opt3: Barak the son of Abinoam of Kedesh-naphtali
opt4: Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it
correct: Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it
explanation: Othniel demonstrated heroic courage in taking the city, marrying Achsah, and later rising under God's Spirit as Israel's first deliverer-judge (Judges 3:9). Joshua 15:17 (KJV) - "And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife."

question: What practical and essential wedding blessing did Achsah request from her father Caleb?
opt1: Give me a blessing; for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water
opt2: Give me forty shekels of gold and ten embroidered garments
opt3: Give me a royal vineyard in the fertile valley of Sorek
opt4: Give me a troop of fifty horsemen to escort my caravan
correct: Give me a blessing; for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water
explanation: Recognizing that arid southern pasture land was useless without water, Achsah wisely petitioned her loving father for vital water sources. Joshua 15:19 (KJV) - "Who answered, Give me a blessing; for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs."

question: How did Caleb respond to his daughter Achsah's request for water?
opt1: He dug a single cistern in the central court of Debir
opt2: And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs
opt3: He gave her the fishing rights along the river Jordan
opt4: He purchased a fountain from the neighboring Kenites
correct: And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs
explanation: Caleb demonstrated generous parental grace, granting her both the elevated mountain springs and the valley springs, ensuring abundant perpetual irrigation. Joshua 15:19 (KJV) - "...And he gave her the upper springs, and the nether springs."

question: Which historic citadel in Judah's northern border could the children of Judah not drive out?
opt1: The fortified seaport of Joppa defended by Philistine galleys
opt2: The royal city of Gezer fortified by King Horam's cavalry
opt3: The Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem: but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day
opt4: The mountain fortress of Beth-zur defended by Amorite archers
correct: The Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem: but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day
explanation: The stronghold of Zion (Jebus/Jerusalem) remained a stubborn Jebusite enclave until King David finally conquered it centuries later (2 Sam 5:6-9). Joshua 15:63 (KJV) - "As for the Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out: but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day."

question: What famous city of palm trees was included in the extensive catalog of Judah's cities in Joshua 15?
opt1: Damascus, renowned for its gardens and rivers of Abana
opt2: Tyre, acclaimed for its purple dyes and merchant navies
opt3: Tadmor, built in the desert wilderness for eastern trade
opt4: Engedi, famous for its freshwater springs and desert oases beside the Salt Sea
correct: Engedi, famous for its freshwater springs and desert oases beside the Salt Sea
explanation: Judah's cities extended across the Negev, the Shephelah, the hill country, and the desert wilderness, including the miraculous oasis of En-gedi. Joshua 15:62 (KJV) - "And Nibshan, and the city of Salt, and En-gedi; six cities with their villages."

question: For which two prominent half-tribes did the second major allotment of land in central Canaan fall?
opt1: The children of Zebulun and Issachar in the northern plain
opt2: The children of Dan and Simeon in the southern desert
opt3: The children of Benjamin and Gad beside the river Jordan
opt4: The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance
correct: The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance
explanation: Joseph received the double portion of the firstborn through his two sons Ephraim and Manasseh, occupying the fertile central mountain backbone of Canaan. Joshua 16:1, 4 (KJV) - "And the lot of the children of Joseph fell from Jordan by Jericho... So the children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, took their inheritance."

question: From what eastern landmark to what western sea did the southern border of Joseph's lot extend?
opt1: From Jordan by Jericho, unto the water of Jericho on the east... and the goings out thereof were at the sea
opt2: From the Red Sea in the south unto the river Euphrates in the north
opt3: From the valley of Eshcol unto the mountains of Seir eastward
opt4: From the brook of Egypt unto the Sea of Chinnereth in Galilee
correct: From Jordan by Jericho, unto the water of Jericho on the east... and the goings out thereof were at the sea
explanation: The border ran from the Jordan River near Jericho across the central plateau to Bethel, descending down the Beth-horon passes to the Mediterranean Sea. Joshua 16:1, 3 (KJV) - "And the lot of the children of Joseph fell from Jordan by Jericho, unto the water of Jericho on the east, to the wilderness... and the goings out thereof were at the sea."

question: Which historic holy place was situated along the southern border of the children of Joseph?
opt1: Kadesh-barnea in the wilderness of Paran
opt2: Bethel, and goeth out from Bethel to Luz
opt3: Beersheba in the southern wilderness
opt4: Mount Sinai in the Arabian desert
correct: Bethel, and goeth out from Bethel to Luz
explanation: Bethel ('House of God'), where Jacob had dreamed of the heavenly ladder (Gen 28), formed a key border boundary between Benjamin and Joseph. Joshua 16:2 (KJV) - "And goeth out from Bethel to Luz, and passeth along unto the borders of Archi to Ataroth,"

question: Which strategic mountain passes did the border descend through toward the western plain?
opt1: Through the passes of Mount Hor near the tomb of Aaron
opt2: Through the defiles of Mount Hermon near the waters of Merom
opt3: Unto the coast of Beth-horon the nether, and to Gezer
opt4: Through the gorge of the river Arnon into the plains of Moab
correct: Unto the coast of Beth-horon the nether, and to Gezer
explanation: The twin towns of Upper and Nether Beth-horon controlled the crucial military highway linking the coastal plain to the central Judean highlands. question: Which river served as the northern boundary marker separating Ephraim's territory from Manasseh?
opt1: The river Kishon flowing into the bay of Acre

Joshua 16:8 (KJV) - "The border went out from Tappuah westward unto the river Kanah; and the goings out thereof were at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim by their families."

question: Where did Ephraim have separate enclave cities situated outside their main borders?
opt1: The separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh

Joshua 16:9 (KJV) - "And the separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages."

question: Which fortified Canaanite city could the tribe of Ephraim not drive out?
opt1: The northern stronghold of Hazor beside the waters of Merom

opt4: The fortress of Jericho near the crossing of Jordan

explanation: Instead of obeying God's command to eradicate Canaanite corruption, Ephraim compromised for economic gain by putting the inhabitants under forced tribute. Joshua 16:10 (KJV) - "...but the Canaanites dwell among the Ephraimites unto this day, and serve under tribute."

question: What spiritual danger arose from allowing Canaanite enclaves like Gezer to remain in the land?
opt1: They drained the fertility of the soil through unholy pagan farming

opt3: They constructed wooden ships that attacked the fishing fleets

question: Who was the maternal ancestor through whom Ephraim and Manasseh were descended from Joseph in Egypt?
opt1: Asenath, the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On, given to Joseph in Egypt

question: Why was the firstborn of Joseph, Manasseh, granted a prominent lot on both sides of Jordan?

Joshua 17:1 (KJV) - "There was also a lot for the tribe of Manasseh; for he was the firstborn of Joseph; to wit, for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead: because he was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan."

question: Which five courageous daughters of Zelophehad stood before the leaders demanding an inheritance?
opt1: Miriam, Deborah, Jael, Huldah, and Athaliah

correct: Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah
explanation: These five sisters demonstrated remarkable faith and legal initiative, ensuring their deceased father's lineage and name would not be blotted out of Israel. Joshua 17:3 (KJV) - "And these are the names of his daughters, Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah."

question: Before which high council did the daughters of Zelophehad present their petition for land?
opt1: Before the seventy military captains of the armed host at Gilgal

Joshua 17:4 (KJV) - "And they came near before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brethren."

question: What righteous judgment did Joshua and Eleazar render in response to the daughters' petition?

question: How many total portions fell to the tribe of Manasseh on the western side of the river Jordan?

question: Which prominent Canaanite city fortress could Manasseh not drive out, resulting in the Canaanites dwelling there?
opt1: Jericho and the cities of the Jordan valley

question: What complaint did the combined house of Joseph bring to Joshua concerning their allotment?
opt1: Our territory is barren desert containing no freshwater springs or wells

Joshua 17:14 (KJV) - "And the children of Joseph spake unto Joshua, saying, Why hast thou given me but one lot and one portion to inherit, seeing I am a great people, forasmuch as the LORD hath blessed me hitherto?"

question: What bold, challenging challenge did Joshua give to the complaining children of Joseph?
opt1: Take half of the territory of Benjamin and drive them into the desert

Joshua 17:15 (KJV) - "And Joshua answered them, If thou be a great people, then get thee up to the wood country, and cut down for thyself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the giants, if mount Ephraim be too narrow for thee."

question: What military obstacle did the children of Joseph fear regarding the Canaanites in the valley?
opt1: All the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both they who are of Beth-shean and they of the valley of Jezreel

opt3: The kings of the valley had forged poison arrows that no armor could resist

Joshua 17:16 (KJV) - "And the children of Joseph said, The hill is not enough for us: and all the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both they who are of Beth-shean and her towns, and they who are of the valley of Jezreel."

question: What inspiring prophetic word did Joshua give Joseph to overcome the Canaanite iron chariots?
opt1: Wait until the rainy season when their heavy iron chariot wheels get stuck in mud

Joshua 17:17-18 (KJV) - "And Joshua spake unto the house of Joseph, even to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, Thou art a great people, and hast great power: thou shalt not have one lot only... for thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots, and though they be strong."

question: At which historic location did the whole congregation assemble to set up the tabernacle of the congregation?
opt1: At Gilgal beside the monument of twelve river stones

Joshua 18:1 (KJV) - "And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there. And the land was subdued before them."

question: How many tribes of Israel had still not received their territorial inheritance when the tabernacle was set up at Shiloh?

question: What piercing rebuke and challenging question did Joshua address to the seven hesitant tribes?

Joshua 18:3 (KJV) - "And Joshua said unto the children of Israel, How long are ye slack to go to possess the land, which the LORD God of your fathers hath given you?"

question: How many survey commissioners from each of the seven remaining tribes was Joshua to appoint?

opt4: Twelve men representing the twelve stones of Gilgal
correct: Give out from among you three men for each tribe (21 men in all)
explanation: Joshua organized a thorough, scholarly topographical commission of twenty-one men (three from each of the seven tribes) to survey and map the uncharted territory. Joshua 18:4 (KJV) - "Give out from among you three men for each tribe: and I will send them, and they shall rise, and go through the land, and describe it according to the inheritance of them; and they shall come again to me."

question: Into how many distinct parts were the surveyors commanded to divide and document the land in a book?

question: Where did the two major tribal blocs, Judah and Joseph, abide while the survey was conducted?

opt4: Both tribes garrisoned the ruins of Jericho and the fortress of Ai

question: Before whom and where did Joshua cast lots to distribute the seven surveyed territories?
opt1: Before the royal assembly of elders in the gate of Hebron

opt4: And Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the LORD

explanation: The casting of lots was conducted with solemn reverence at the door of the Tabernacle before God's holy presence, acknowledging God's direct sovereignty. Joshua 18:10 (KJV) - "And Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the LORD: and there Joshua divided the land unto the children of Israel according to their divisions."

question: Which tribe's lot came up first among the seven surveyed portions in Shiloh?
opt1: The lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up according to their families

Joshua 18:11 (KJV) - "And the lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up according to their families: and the coast of their lot came forth between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph."

question: Between the territories of which two powerful tribes did the border of Benjamin fall?
opt1: Between the maritime tribe of Dan and the pastures of Asher

Joshua 18:11 (KJV) - "...and the coast of their lot came forth between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph."

question: Which prominent royal citadel was listed among the cities of Benjamin in Joshua 18:28?

Joshua 18:28 (KJV) - "And Zelah, Eleph, and Jebusi, which is Jerusalem, Gibeath, and Kirjath; fourteen cities with their villages. question: Why was the territory of the tribe of Simeon taken out of the portion originally allotted to Judah?
opt1: Because the Simeonites had conquered the southern desert fortresses alone

opt3: Because Moses had decreed that Simeon should rule over all the Negev pastures
opt4: For the part of the children of Judah was too much for them: therefore the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them
correct: For the part of the children of Judah was too much for them: therefore the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them
explanation: Judah's initial allotment proved disproportionately large for their numbers, so covenant equity prompted the peaceful sharing of southern towns with Simeon. Joshua 19:9 (KJV) - "Out of the portion of the children of Judah was the inheritance of the children of Simeon: for the part of the children of Judah was too much for them: therefore the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them."

question: Which northern tribe received the third lot, with its border reaching unto Sarid and Mount Tabor?
opt1: The children of Zebulun according to their families

question: Which exceptionally fertile valley and famous royal city was included in the fourth lot for Issachar?

Joshua 19:17-18 (KJV) - "And the fourth lot came out to Issachar, for the children of Issachar according to their families. And their border was toward Jezreel, and Chesulloth, and Shunem,"

question: Which maritime coastal territory extending from Mount Carmel northward unto great Zidon fell to Asher?
opt1: The lot of the tribe of Naphtali across the mountain peaks

opt4: The lot of the tribe of Simeon in the wilderness of Beersheba

explanation: Asher received the rich Phoenician coastal plain, abundant in olive oil, trade, and maritime commerce (fulfilling Gen 49:20 and Deut 33:24). Joshua 19:24, 26, 28 (KJV) - "And the fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families... and reacheth to Carmel westward... and unto great Zidon;"

question: Which northern tribe received the sixth lot, containing fenced cities around the Sea of Chinnereth?
opt1: The children of Judah in the wilderness of Zin

question: Why did the children of Dan march northward to fight against Leshem and capture it?

opt4: Because an altar of solid gold was discovered hidden beneath the ruins of Leshem

explanation: Pressed into the foothills by the Amorites and Philistines (Judges 1:34), Dan migrated north to conquer Leshem (Laish) near the headwaters of the Jordan. Joshua 19:47 (KJV) - "And the coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them: therefore the children of Dan went up to fight against Leshem, and took it, and smote it with the edge of the sword, and possessed it, and dwelt therein..."

question: What new name did the children of Dan give unto the captured northern city of Leshem?
opt1: They named it Gilgal in memory of the crossing of Jordan

opt4: They named it Bethel in remembrance of Jacob's holy altar

question: What specific city in Mount Ephraim did the congregation give unto Joshua as his personal inheritance?

question: At what sacred location did Eleazar, Joshua, and the tribal heads conclude the dividing of the land?

Joshua 19:51 (KJV) - "These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes... divided for an inheritance by lot in Shiloh before the LORD, at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. question: What was the primary divine purpose for establishing the cities of refuge in Joshua 20?

Joshua 20:2-3 (KJV) - "Appoint out for you cities of refuge, whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses: That the slayer that killeth any person unawares and unwittingly may flee thither: and they shall be your refuge from the avenger of blood."

question: What was the fugitive manslayer required to do upon arriving at the gate of a city of refuge?

opt4: Shave his head and remain in solitary confinement for forty days

Joshua 20:4 (KJV) - "And when he that doth flee unto one of those cities shall stand at the entering of the gate of the city, and shall declare his cause in the ears of the elders of that city, they shall take him into the city unto them, and give him a place, that he may dwell among them."

Joshua 20:6 (KJV) - "And he shall dwell in that city, until he stand before the congregation for judgment, and until the death of the high priest that shall be in those days: then shall the slayer return, and come unto his own city..."

question: Which northern city in Galilee was sanctified as a city of refuge in the territory of Naphtali?

explanation: Kedesh ('Holy Place') provided accessible mountain refuge for the northernmost regions of the promised land. Joshua 20:7 (KJV) - "And they appointed Kedesh in Galilee in mount Naphtali, and Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah."

question: Which central city between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim was sanctified as a city of refuge?

opt2: Shiloh before the tabernacle
opt3: Samaria upon its central hill
opt4: Shechem in mount Ephraim

explanation: Shechem, situated in the heart of central Canaan, offered easy geographical access for anyone fleeing from the central tribes. Joshua 20:7 (KJV) - "...and Shechem in mount Ephraim..."

opt3: Jerusalem in the border of Benjamin
opt4: Bethlehem in the hill country of Judea
correct: Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah
explanation: Hebron served as the southern haven of refuge, strategically located high in the Judean mountains for swift access. Joshua 20:7 (KJV) - "...and Kirjath-arba, which is Hebron, in the mountain of Judah."

question: Which three cities of refuge were appointed on the west side of Jordan in Canaan proper?
opt1: Jericho in the valley, Bethel on the heights, and Gilgal by the river
opt2: Kedesh in Galilee, Shechem in mount Ephraim, and Kirjath-arba (Hebron) in the mountain of Judah
