explanation: These three western cities were evenly distributed from north to south (Galilee, Ephraim, Judah), ensuring that no citizen was more than a half-day's journey from safety. Joshua 20:7 (KJV).

question: Which city of refuge was appointed east of Jordan out of the tribe of Reuben in the plain?

opt2: Medeba on the southern plateau
opt3: Bezer in the wilderness upon the plain out of the tribe of Reuben
opt4: Aroer on the bank of the river Arnon

explanation: Bezer served the southern Transjordan tribes from its high tableland position in Reuben's territory. Joshua 20:8 (KJV) - "And on the other side Jordan by Jericho eastward, they assigned Bezer in the wilderness upon the plain out of the tribe of Reuben..."

question: Which city of refuge was appointed east of Jordan out of the tribe of Gad in Gilead?
opt1: Jazer in the border of Ammon
opt2: Mahanaim where the angels met Jacob
opt3: Succoth beside the river Jabbok
opt4: Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad
correct: Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad
explanation: Ramoth-gilead ('Heights of Gilead') was an elevated fortress refuge for the central Transjordan region. Joshua 20:8 (KJV) - "...and Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad..."

question: Which city of refuge was appointed east of Jordan out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan?
opt1: Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh

opt4: Salcah on the far eastern frontier
correct: Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh
explanation: Golan provided refuge for the expansive northern pastureland of Bashan, completing the six perfectly situated sanctuary cities across Israel. Joshua 20:8 (KJV) - "...and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh."

question: How many total cities, with their surrounding pasture suburbs, were granted unto the Levites?

Joshua 21:41 (KJV) - "All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Israel were forty and eight cities with their suburbs."

question: How many cities fell by lot to the priestly sons of Aaron out of the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin?

Joshua 21:4, 19 (KJV) - "...and the children of Aaron the priest, which were of the Levites, had by lot out of the tribe of Judah, and out of the tribe of Simeon, and out of the tribe of Benjamin, thirteen cities."

question: Which three major branches of the tribe of Levi received cities throughout the tribes?
opt1: The Aaronites, the Phinehasites, and the Zadokites

question: How many cities were allotted to the families of the children of Gershon out of the northern and eastern tribes?
opt1: Ten cities out of the tribe of Ephraim and Dan
opt2: Twelve cities out of Reuben and the house of Gad
opt3: Eight cities out of the territory of Judah and Simeon
opt4: Thirteen cities out of the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan
correct: Thirteen cities out of the tribes of Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan
explanation: The Gershonites served in the northern regions and northern Transjordan, receiving thirteen dedicated cities. Joshua 21:6 (KJV) - "And the children of Gershon had by lot out of the families of the tribe of Issachar, and out of the tribe of Asher, and out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities."

question: How many cities were granted unto the children of Merari by their families out of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun?
opt1: Twelve cities out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun

Joshua 21:7 (KJV) - "The children of Merari by their families had out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities."

question: What surrounded each of the forty-eight Levitical cities to support their livestock and herds?
opt1: High stone defensive walls equipped with iron watchtowers

opt4: Sacred groves of oak trees dedicated to incense offerings

question: What covenant declaration does Joshua 21:43 record concerning God giving Israel the promised land?
opt1: And Israel conquered half of the land while the rest was lost through compromise
opt2: And the land was given on condition of paying annual tribute to Egypt
opt3: And the LORD gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein

correct: And the LORD gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein
explanation: The narrative highlights the total fidelity of God: every square mile promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was delivered into their hands. Joshua 21:43 (KJV) - "And the LORD gave unto Israel all the land which he sware to give unto their fathers; and they possessed it, and dwelt therein."

question: What divine blessing did the LORD give them round about regarding their enemies?
opt1: The LORD gave them continuous warfare for fifty consecutive years
opt2: The LORD commanded them to build fortified castles on every hilltop

opt4: And the LORD gave them rest round about, according to all that he sware unto their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them
correct: And the LORD gave them rest round about, according to all that he sware unto their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them
explanation: God granted them complete rest and peace on every border, proving that when God's people walk in obedience, no adversary can withstand them. Joshua 21:44 (KJV) - "And the LORD gave them rest round about, according to all that he sware unto their fathers: and there stood not a man of all their enemies before them; the LORD delivered all their enemies into their hand."

question: What magnificent declaration of God's complete and unfailing faithfulness is recorded in Joshua 21:45?
opt1: There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass

correct: There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass

Joshua 21:45 (KJV) - "There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass."

question: What spiritual lesson does the fulfillment of Joshua 21:45 provide for believers in every generation?

opt4: Spiritual victory is guaranteed only to those of physical Hebrew biological descent
correct: God is absolutely true to His Word: His promises never fail, and those who trust Him will see every covenant promise fulfilled in His perfect time
explanation: This verse anchors the believer's faith across all ages, assuring us that our covenant God is eternally reliable and keeps every promise He speaks. Joshua 21:45 (KJV).

question: What commendation did Joshua speak unto the two and a half eastern tribes before releasing them home?
opt1: Ye have been slow to battle and failed to support the southern armies of Judah

opt4: Ye must remain another seven years to build stone roads across Canaan
correct: Ye have kept all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you... and have not left your brethren these many days
explanation: Joshua praised Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh for their exemplary covenant loyalty, having fought alongside their western brethren through years of arduous campaign. Joshua 22:2-3 (KJV) - "And said unto them, Ye have kept all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and have obeyed my voice in all that I commanded you: Ye have not left your brethren these many days unto this day, but have kept the charge of the commandment of the LORD your God."

question: What solemn charge did Joshua deliver unto the returning eastern tribes in Joshua 22:5?
opt1: Build high defensive palisades on the eastern bank of Jordan against the Ammonites
opt2: Collect annual tribute from the nomadic desert tribes to send to Shiloh
opt3: Take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law... to love the LORD your God, and to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul

explanation: Joshua emphasized wholehearted inward devotion above outward ritual, charging them to love God, cleave to Him, and obey His holy law with all their heart and soul. Joshua 22:5 (KJV) - "But take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law, which Moses the servant of the LORD charged you, to love the LORD your God, and to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and to cleave unto him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul."

question: With what great riches did Joshua dismiss the eastern warriors back to their tents across Jordan?

explanation: Joshua blessed them as they returned laden with immense spoils of war, instructing them to share the abundance generously with those who had guarded their homes. Joshua 22:8 (KJV) - "And he spake unto them, saying, Return with much riches unto your tents, and with very much cattle, with silver, and with gold, and with brass, and with iron, and with very much raiment: divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren."

question: What imposing monument did the children of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh construct by the river Jordan?
opt1: Built there an altar by Jordan, a great altar to see to

opt4: A fortified border watchtower garrisoned by a thousand archers

Joshua 22:10 (KJV) - "And when they came unto the borders of Jordan, that are in the land of Canaan, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by Jordan, a great altar to see to."

question: How did the western congregation of Israel initially react upon hearing of the great altar by Jordan?

Joshua 22:12 (KJV) - "And when the children of Israel heard of it, the whole congregation of the children of Israel gathered themselves together at Shiloh, to go up to war against them."

question: Who was appointed to lead the fact-finding delegation sent to confront the eastern tribes?

Joshua 22:13-14 (KJV) - "And the children of Israel sent unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead, Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, And with him ten princes, of each chief house a prince throughout all the tribes of Israel;"

question: Which two past national sins did Phinehas cite to warn the eastern tribes of the danger of rebellion?

explanation: Phinehas warned that corporate sin brings corporate wrath, reminding them how Achan's secret sin caused thirty-six men to die and Peor's plague killed twenty-four thousand. Joshua 22:17, 20 (KJV) - "Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us... Did not Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the accursed thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel? and that man perished not alone in his iniquity."

question: What passionate, solemn oath did the eastern tribes proclaim in vindicating their innocence?

Joshua 22:22 (KJV) - "The LORD God of gods, the LORD God of gods, he knoweth, and Israel he shall know; if it be in rebellion, or if in transgression against the LORD, (save us not this day,)"

question: What was the true, beautiful motive of the eastern tribes in building the altar by the Jordan?

opt4: To mark a permanent national border separating two completely distinct nations

Joshua 22:26-27 (KJV) - "Therefore we said, Let us now make preparation to build us an altar, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice: But that it may be a witness between us, and you, and our generations after us, that we might do the service of the LORD before him with our burnt offerings..."

question: What name did the children of Reuben and Gad give to the altar, and what was its meaning?

explanation: The altar was named 'Ed' (Hebrew for 'Witness'), standing as an unshakeable monument that both eastern and western tribes worship the one true God in holy unity. Joshua 22:34 (KJV) - "And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar Ed: for it shall be a witness between us that the LORD is God."

question: Whom did Joshua summon together when he was old and stricken in age in chapter 23?
opt1: He summoned the kings of Egypt and Babylon to sign a treaty of non-aggression

Joshua 23:2 (KJV) - "And Joshua called for all Israel, and for their elders, and for their heads, and for their judges, and for their officers, and said unto them, I am old and stricken in age:"

question: To whom did Joshua ascribe all the glory and credit for Israel's military triumphs in Canaan?
opt1: Unto his own strategic genius and the bravery of his thirty captains

opt4: For the LORD your God is he that hath fought for you, as he hath promised you

Joshua 23:3, 10 (KJV) - "And ye have seen all that the LORD your God hath done unto all these nations because of you; for the LORD your God is he that hath fought for you."

question: What courageous charge did Joshua give regarding the book of the law of Moses in Joshua 23:6?

opt4: Permit each tribe to interpret the commandments according to their own judgment

Joshua 23:6 (KJV) - "Be ye therefore very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that ye turn not aside therefrom to the right hand or to the left;"

question: What strict prohibitions did Joshua issue concerning the pagan gods of the remaining nations?

Joshua 23:7 (KJV) - "That ye come not among these nations, these that remain among you; neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow yourselves unto them:"

question: What positive spiritual command did Joshua urge them to practice toward the LORD their God?

question: What astonishing military ratio did Joshua declare would manifest when God fights for His people?

Joshua 23:10 (KJV) - "One man of you shall chase a thousand: for the LORD your God, he it is that fighteth for you, as he hath promised you."

question: What personal spiritual responsibility did Joshua command each individual to take heed unto in Joshua 23:11?

opt4: Take heed to build palaces in each tribal capital for the judges

opt3: They shall enrich Israel's treasury with unlimited maritime trade from Tyre
opt4: They shall teach Israel superior methods of iron smelting and vineyard cultivation
correct: They shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land
explanation: Spiritual compromise with ungodliness always leads to spiritual ruin: remaining Canaanites would become painful scourges and blinding thorns, leading to loss of the land. Joshua 23:12-13 (KJV) - "...know for a certainty that the LORD your God will no more drive out any of these nations from before you; but they shall be snares and traps unto you, and scourges in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until ye perish from off this good land which the LORD your God hath given you."

question: What personal dying testimony did Joshua declare concerning God's faithfulness in Joshua 23:14?
opt1: I have fought a good fight, and now I bequeath my spear unto the prince of Judah
opt2: My strength is exhausted and many promises remain incomplete for future ages
opt3: Behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth: and ye know in all your hearts... that not one thing hath failed of all the good things which the LORD your God spake concerning you; all are come to pass
opt4: I command you to bury me in the cave of Machpelah beside father Abraham
correct: Behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth: and ye know in all your hearts... that not one thing hath failed of all the good things which the LORD your God spake concerning you; all are come to pass
explanation: Facing eternity ('going the way of all the earth'), Joshua delivered a resounding personal witness: God's Word is 100% reliable; not a single good promise ever failed. Joshua 23:14 (KJV) - "And, behold, this day I am going the way of all the earth: and ye know in all your hearts and in all your souls, that not one thing hath failed of all the good things which the LORD your God spake concerning you; all are come to pass unto you, and not one thing hath failed thereof."

question: Just as every good promise came to pass, what did Joshua solemnly warn would happen if Israel transgressed the covenant?
opt1: God would overlook their idolatry because of His covenant with Abraham
opt2: The land would continue to yield corn and wine regardless of their sins
opt3: God would send angels to fight for them even if they bowed down unto Baal
opt4: So shall the LORD bring upon you all evil things, until he have destroyed you from off this good land which the LORD your God hath given you
correct: So shall the LORD bring upon you all evil things, until he have destroyed you from off this good land which the LORD your God hath given you
explanation: God's holiness guarantees that covenant warnings are just as real and certain as covenant blessings: unrepentant apostasy would inevitably bring exile and judgment. Joshua 23:15-16 (KJV) - "Therefore it shall come to pass, that as all good things are come upon you... so shall the LORD bring upon you all evil things, until he have destroyed you from off this good land..."

question: At which momentous location did Joshua gather all the tribes of Israel for his final covenant renewal?
opt1: At the stone monument pitched in the camp of Gilgal
opt2: At the sanctuary of the tabernacle pitched in Shiloh
opt3: Upon the summit of Mount Moriah in Jerusalem
opt4: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and called for the elders of Israel
correct: And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and called for the elders of Israel
explanation: Shechem was steeped in sacred history: here Abraham first built an altar in Canaan (Gen 12:6-7), Jacob buried idols under an oak (Gen 35:4), and Israel recited the blessings and curses (Josh 8). Joshua 24:1 (KJV) - "And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and called for the elders of Israel, and for their heads, and for their judges, and for their officers; and they presented themselves before God."

question: Beyond what river did Abraham's ancestors dwell in ancient times, and what did they worship?
opt1: On the other side of the flood (Euphrates river) in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham... and they served other gods
opt2: Beyond the river Nile in Egypt, where they worshipped the sacred golden calf
opt3: Along the river Jordan in Canaan, where they sacrificed to the Amorite deities
opt4: Beside the brook of Egypt in the desert, where they worshipped the sun and moon
correct: On the other side of the flood (Euphrates river) in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham... and they served other gods
explanation: Joshua reminded Israel of sovereign grace: God called Abraham out of pagan idolatry in Ur of the Chaldees beyond the Euphrates River ('the flood') to make him a father of faith. Joshua 24:2 (KJV) - "And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods."

question: What divine weapon did God send before Israel to drive out the two kings of the Amorites, not by human sword or bow?
opt1: A consuming pillar of fire that incinerated their wooden chariots
opt2: And I sent the hornet before you, which drave them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; but not with thy sword, nor with thy bow
opt3: A plague of biting serpents that overran their fortified mountain citadels
opt4: An army of ten thousand angels carrying flaming double-edged swords
correct: And I sent the hornet before you, which drave them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; but not with thy sword, nor with thy bow
explanation: God used supernatural means—the 'hornet' (symbolizing divine panic and stinging judgment)—to clear the land, reminding Israel that salvation belongs unto the LORD alone. Joshua 24:12 (KJV) - "And I sent the hornet before you, which drave them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; but not with thy sword, nor with thy bow."

question: What grace did God bestow upon Israel in giving them Canaan, according to Joshua 24:13?
opt1: Gold and silver mined from the depths of Mount Sinai in the desert
opt2: Fleets of cedar merchant ships trading with the distant ports of Tarshish
opt3: A land for which ye did not labour, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them; of the vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat
opt4: Immunity from all physical disease, aging, and bodily infirmity
correct: A land for which ye did not labour, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them; of the vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat
explanation: Canaan was a profound type of salvation by grace: Israel inherited fully-built cities, dug cisterns, and productive vineyards that they had neither built nor planted. Joshua 24:13 (KJV) - "And I have given you a land for which ye did not labour, and cities which ye built not, and ye dwell in them; of the vineyards and oliveyards which ye planted not do ye eat."

question: What immortal challenge and resolute confession did Joshua speak unto all the people in Joshua 24:15?
opt1: Let each man do that which is right in his own eyes until a king is anointed
opt2: Worship the gods of Egypt in private while honouring the LORD in the public gate
opt3: Appoint a council of twelve judges to determine whether Baal or the LORD is greater
opt4: Choose you this day whom ye will serve... but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD
correct: Choose you this day whom ye will serve... but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD
explanation: One of the most celebrated declarations in Scripture: Joshua confronted the people with the urgency of decisive personal and family consecration to serve the living God. Joshua 24:15 (KJV) - "And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD."

question: How did the congregation resoundingly respond to Joshua's covenant challenge?
opt1: God forbid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods; For the LORD our God, he it is that brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt
opt2: We desire to worship both the LORD and the fertility gods of the Amorites
opt3: Let us return to the fertile fields of Goshen across the Red Sea in Egypt
opt4: We cannot render an answer until our elders consult the signs in the stars
correct: God forbid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods; For the LORD our God, he it is that brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt
explanation: The people affirmed their covenant loyalty, recalling how God had delivered them from Egyptian bondage, preserved them through the wilderness, and driven out the nations. Joshua 24:16-18 (KJV) - "And the people answered and said, God forbid that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods; For the LORD our God, he it is that brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt... therefore will we also serve the LORD; for he is our God."

question: What physical monument did Joshua set up under an oak by the sanctuary as an enduring covenant witness?
opt1: A bronze serpent raised on a cedar pole before the congregation
opt2: He took a great stone, and set it up there under an oak, that was by the sanctuary of the LORD
opt3: The outstretched spear with which he had signaled the conquest of Ai
opt4: A golden seven-branched lampstand filled with consecrated olive oil
correct: He took a great stone, and set it up there under an oak, that was by the sanctuary of the LORD
explanation: Joshua erected a massive stone pillar under the ancient oak at Shechem, declaring that the stone itself had heard all the words of the LORD and stood as a perpetual witness. Joshua 24:26-27 (KJV) - "And Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God, and took a great stone, and set it up there under an oak, that was by the sanctuary of the LORD. And Joshua said unto all the people, Behold, this stone shall be a witness unto us; for it hath heard all the words of the LORD..."

question: How old was Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, when he finished his earthly race?
opt1: One hundred and twenty years old, like Moses on Mount Nebo
opt2: Eighty-five years old, like Caleb conquering Hebron
opt3: An hundred and ten years old (110 years old)
opt4: Ninety-nine years old, like Abraham receiving the covenant
correct: An hundred and ten years old (110 years old)
explanation: Joshua lived to the venerable age of 110 (the exact age of Joseph in Gen 50:26), bearing the supreme title of honour: 'the servant of the LORD.' Joshua 24:29 (KJV) - "And it came to pass after these things, that Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, being an hundred and ten years old."

question: Where was Joshua buried in the border of his inheritance?
opt1: In the cave of Machpelah near Hebron beside the patriarchs
opt2: On the lonely summit of Mount Nebo across the river Jordan
opt3: In the valley of Achor beneath a great cairn of stones
opt4: In Timnath-serah, which is in mount Ephraim, on the north side of the hill of Gaash
correct: In Timnath-serah, which is in mount Ephraim, on the north side of the hill of Gaash
explanation: Joshua was laid to rest in his own humble estate at Timnath-serah in Mount Ephraim, honored by the nation he had led into the promised rest. Joshua 24:30 (KJV) - "And they buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath-serah, which is in mount Ephraim, on the north side of the hill of Gaash."

question: Whose bones, brought up out of Egypt centuries earlier, were finally buried at Shechem in fulfilled prophecy?
opt1: The bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem
opt2: The bones of Aaron the first high priest of Israel
opt3: The bones of Miriam the prophetess from Kadesh
opt4: The bones of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite
correct: The bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem
explanation: Centuries after Joseph died in Egypt making Israel swear to carry his bones to Canaan (Gen 50:25, Heb 11:22), his bones found their final resting place in Jacob's parcel of ground at Shechem. Joshua 24:32 (KJV) - "And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph."
